title: Conditional Compilation
concept: Conditional compilation selectively includes or excludes code depending on the build environment.

steps.title: Include stdio.h header
steps.explanation:
**`#include <stdio.h>`** — Include headers for `printf` use.

In this lesson you will learn **Conditional Compilation**.

steps.title: Compile condition switch definition
steps.explanation: **`#define DEBUG_MODE 1`** — A macro that acts as a **switch** that determines what code the `#ifdef` and `#if` directives below will include. Changing this value or deleting the line itself will cause debug code to be excluded from compilation.

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation: **`int main() {`** — The program entry point. At this point, the preprocessor has already completed inserting headers, defining macros, and including/removing code based on `#ifdef`/`#if` conditions.

steps.title: first output
steps.explanation: **`printf("Program Start\n");`** — It is not part of any `#ifdef` or `#if` block, so it will compile and run **always** regardless of its conditions. `"Program Start"` is displayed.

steps.title: Conditional compilation 1: #ifdef
steps.explanation: **`#ifdef DEBUG_MODE`** — Checks whether `DEBUG_MODE` is **defined**. True if `#defined` with any value, false if undefined.

steps.title: Run debug code
steps.explanation: **`printf("[DEBUG] Variable `"[DEBUG] Variable x checking..."` is output.

steps.title: Conditional compilation 2: #if
steps.explanation: **`#if DEBUG_MODE == 0`** — Unlike `#ifdef`, the **values ​​of the macro are compared directly**. `#ifdef` only checks for existence, whereas `#if` evaluates the value of the expression to determine whether it is true or false.

steps.title: last output
steps.explanation:
**`printf("Program End\n");`** — Always executes because it is outside a conditional block.

quiz.question: What is the main reason to use Header Guard (#ifndef HEADER_H ...)?
options: Prevent duplicate header file inclusion (prevent redefinition errors)
quiz.explanation:
If you include the same header multiple times in one source file (directly or indirectly), a compilation error will occur due to overlapping structures or functions.
Header Guard prevents this.

misconceptions.wrong: Code excluded with #ifdef is checked like an if statement at runtime.
misconceptions.correct:
There isn't even any condition checking at runtime.
The code itself either disappears or remains during the preprocessing step.
misconceptions.why: It affects the executable size itself.

keyTakeaway: Conditional compilation allows you to create separate debug, release, and OS-specific (Windows/Linux) executables from a single source code.
